title: Security posture discovery with Odin Health
summary: Intro discovery focused on compliance and data residency for ePHI. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention and access, encryption/KMS and BYOK, and data retention policies for clinical data. Agreed next steps to share SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and schedule a technical deep dive for Dedicated/Private options.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Data residency and retention for ePHI
action_items: Maya Chen: share SOC2 report, ISO summary, and security whitepaper (due 2026-08-03)
Alex Rivera: send Dedicated/Private architecture diagram and propose a deep-dive time (due 2026-08-05)
Marcus Lee: provide specific data retention & ePHI handling requirements (due 2026-08-06)
Tara Singh: share a list of endpoints that need VPC egress controls for the PoC (due 2026-08-06)
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 and ISO artifacts + security whitepaper
Schedule 60m technical deep dive focused on Dedicated/Private deployment and KMS/BYOK options
Agree on PoC scope and success criteria (latency SLO, throughput, data isolation)
Provide preliminary pricing for Dedicated capacity and Private deployment options
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Rivera (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Patel (CTO - Odin Health), Marcus Lee (Head of Security - Odin), Tara Singh (SRE - Odin), Evan Cole (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on security posture, compliance needs for ePHI, and high-level options for hosting.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, i'll hand over to alex shortly to dig into the tech questions but first maybe quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Priya Patel: priya here, cto at odin, we run a clinical notes/triage product, lots of ephi, want to understand how you handle security and where we'd need dedicated/private setups
[00:25] Marcus Lee: marcus, head of security, i'll focus on compliance and encryption stuff
[00:30] Alex Rivera: great, alex from redwood infra, i'll cover runtime and deployment options, also KMS and logs
[00:36] Tara Singh: tara, sres, i'll be the one running the PoC if we move forward
[00:40] Evan Cole: evan from product, interested in timeline and cost tradeoffs
[00:45] Maya Chen: thanks. to kick off, can you tell us current stack and constraints, priya?
[00:52] Dr. Priya Patel: sure, we host in GCP, all patient data in a HIPAA boundary, we use internal idp (okta), SSO already in place, primary requirement is that any vendor handling ephi be either in our VPC or provide strong isolation and auditability. we also need SOC 2 type II and ideally ISO 27001.
[01:12] Marcus Lee: also retention policies: clinical notes stored for seven years, we need logs that show who accessed what and when, and those logs themselves need retention for 3+ years.
[01:25] Alex Rivera: okay that helps. on Redwood side, we operate hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc/on-prem). Hosted is simplest but for ePHI you folks probably look at Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and customer tenancy, Private gives you a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem. both can be configured for stricter networking.
[01:46] Marcus Lee: can you confirm SOC2 and ISO posture? do you have attestations?
[01:52] Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 cert - we'll share the latest artifacts. also a security whitepaper that outlines encryption and logging controls.
[02:03] Marcus Lee: good. what about SSO? our idp is okta and we need SAML 2.0 + SCIM for provisioning.
[02:12] Alex Rivera: we support SAML SSO integrations and SCIM for user provisioning. for Dedicated and Private you can configure SSO to the Redwood console; for hosted api usage keys are still required for service-to-service but console access integrates with SSO. there can be some subtle mapping around RBAC roles, we map idp groups to console roles.
[02:34] Tara Singh: RBAC detail - can we have least-privilege roles? e.g., SREs can deploy instances but not see raw customer data, product can see usage metrics but not logs with PII.
[02:45] Alex Rivera: yes, our RBAC supports fine-grained roles: admin, infra, auditor, read-only, and custom roles. for Private/Dedicated we can restrict access further and supports separation by project/tenant, and we can integrate with your SAML group claims to map to those roles.
[03:03] Dr. Priya Patel: audit logs - what do they contain? are they immutable and can they be exported to our SIEM?
[03:11] Alex Rivera: audit logs include API calls, console actions, model version rollouts, access events, and admin actions. They are write-once within our system and can be streamed to your logging endpoint (e.g., BigQuery, Cloud Storage, or your SIEM via syslog). retention configurable depending on plan; for Dedicated/Private we can push logs directly into your GCS or onto your SIEM with the retention you need.
[03:36] Marcus Lee: and you mentioned "write-once" but we need tamper-evidence - are logs signed or do you offer append-only storage?
[03:43] Alex Rivera: for Private you control the storage so you can choose immutable buckets or WORM policies; for Dedicated we offer append-only logs with cryptographic hashes for tamper-evidence and can provide hash manifests on request. we'll include more specifics in the security pack we send.
[04:00] Evan Cole: encryption - at rest and in transit? and KMS options, BYOK?
[04:06] Alex Rivera: TLS 1.2+ in transit, all data at rest encrypted. For Hosted we manage keys via cloud KMS; we also support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in Dedicated and Private setups and integrations with customer KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, and HSM options). For Private you can fully manage keys in your environment.
[04:28] Marcus Lee: do you support envelope encryption or per-tenant keys?
[04:32] Alex Rivera: yes, per-tenant keys is possible in Dedicated and Private, and we can implement envelope encryption for model caches and artifacts. we'll outline patterns and impacts in the deep-dive.
[04:45] Dr. Priya Patel: data residency - we need data to stay in GCP us-central and can't cross regions for backups without explicit approval.
[04:55] Maya Chen: we have region pinning for deployments, and Dedicated/Private can be restricted to specific regions and clouds. Hosted has regional endpoints as well but backups for hosted may go to replicated regions by default - we'll call that out in the doc we share.
[05:10] Tara Singh: what about data retention and deletion? say we need to purge training cache or KV cache of prompts after 30 days, can you guarantee deletion?
[05:19] Alex Rivera: yes, retention policies can be configured. for Dedicated/Private you get stronger guarantees; we can purge KV caches and any persisted artefacts on a schedule and provide deletion receipts. for hosted customers we have retention defaults but we also offer contracts with specific retention SLAs.
[05:36] Marcus Lee: do you retain any PII in logs or for model telemetry?
[05:41] Alex Rivera: we scrub PII at collection points for telemetry, and logs that contain request/response payloads are redacted by default; for Dedicated/Private we can tune what is collected and can disable storage of request payloads if required.
[05:56] Dr. Priya Patel: okay, how about penetration tests and third-party attestations?
[06:02] Maya Chen: we do annual pentests and use third-party auditors; the SOC2 report includes details, and we can share a redacted pentest summary.
[06:10] Evan Cole: timeline - if we wanted to pilot, how long to get dedicated reserved capacity or private deployment?
[06:16] Alex Rivera: Dedicated reserved pools can be provisioned in weeks (2-4) depending on capacity; Private (VPC-hosted) is a longer project (4-8 weeks) depending on network approvals and certificate exchanges. PoC can start quicker if you accept hosted with scoped isolation for testing, but for ePHI you'd likely want Dedicated or Private for production.
[06:37] Tara Singh: for the PoC we'll need network allowlist, egress rules, and a test dataset that's scrubbed of PHI to validate latency - we'll send that list.
[06:46] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll send SOC2/ISO, security whitepaper, a high-level Dedicated/Private architecture and a proposed deep-dive timeslot. Also preliminary pricing for Dedicated and Private options.
[06:57] Marcus Lee: one more - incident response: how fast do you notify customers and what data you share?
[07:03] Alex Rivera: we have an incident response playbook with SLA-based notifications; we notify customers within defined windows (we'll attach IR playbook section) and provide the scope, impact, and remediation steps. for enterprise contracts we can agree on faster notification windows.
[07:20] Dr. Priya Patel: good. any third-party sub-processors we should be aware of?
[07:25] Maya Chen: we maintain a subprocessor list and will include it - major cloud providers and some monitoring tools; for Dedicated/Private we can minimize subprocessors and there's an option to white-list.
[07:36] Evan Cole: pricing tradeoffs - roughly how much of a premium is Dedicated vs Hosted?
[07:41] Maya Chen: Dedicated is a commit/seat or capacity model and typically a 2-3x premium vs shared hosted per-unit compute but gives predictability and isolation. Private has additional engineering/setup fees. we'll send a ballpark sheet.
[07:56] Tara Singh: last ops Q: can we export a full audit trail if regulators ask for it?
[08:02] Alex Rivera: yes, exports to GCS/your SIEM are supported and we can provide export packages on request. for Private you control retention and exports fully.
[08:14] Maya Chen: OK, let's recap next steps.
[08:17] Marcus Lee: recap?
[08:18] Maya Chen: we'll send SOC2/ISO and security docs; alex will send architecture and schedule deep dive; odin team to send retention and network lists; agree PoC scope and we follow up with pricing.
[08:29] Dr. Priya Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone
[08:31] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and proposed times

[08:40] End of recording.
notes: Call had natural transcription artifacts - some proper nouns simplified, occasional timestamp drift. Customer strongly leaning toward Dedicated initially, Private for long-term compliance if timelines allow.
